headline: Chips Crack While the Rest of the Market Shrugs and Rotates
body_html:
Friday's session ended looking calm on the surface and uneven underneath. Of the 666 stocks in our universe, 338 rose and 324 fell, a near-even split. That hid a heavy loss in semiconductors, which dropped 3.6%, the worst showing among our nine sectors by a wide margin.

The selling reached well past the biggest chip names. AMD fell 8.75%, power-chip maker Alpha and Omega gave up 10.91%, chip-software firm PDF Solutions lost 9.01%, and optical supplier Fabrinet shed 7.51%. Financials slid 1.41% and materials fell 0.8%. Money moved toward consumer stocks, up 0.97%, and energy, up 0.91%, with homebuilders and industrials also finishing higher.

The day's standout mover was Modine Manufacturing, which jumped 27.95%. Engineering firm Stantec added 14%. On the downside, Heartflow sank 19.13%. The session showed that a flat-looking tape can hold a sharp reshuffling of leadership. Traders return Monday, November 16, with chips the first place to look for a bounce or a further slide.

briefs.headline: Chip weakness spreads across the supply chain
briefs.body: Semiconductors fell 3.6% as a group, and the pain reached equipment-adjacent and component names. Alpha and Omega lost 10.91%, PDF Solutions dropped 9.01%, and Fabrinet fell 7.51%. The pattern suggests investors were trimming the whole theme, not just one company.

briefs.headline: Modine's 28% surge leads industrial gainers
briefs.body: Modine Manufacturing, a thermal-management maker, rose 27.95% to lead all gainers in our universe. Engineering-services firm Stantec climbed 14%. Industrials as a sector gained a more modest 0.36%, so the moves were stock-specific.

briefs.headline: Healthcare is flat, but two names move hard
briefs.body: The healthcare sector finished up just 0.07%, yet single stocks swung widely. Drug-packaging supplier Stevanato rose 10.03%, while diagnostics company Heartflow tumbled 19.13%, the steepest decline in our universe.

briefs.headline: Oil outlook tilts toward surplus as Gulf supply returns
briefs.body: The International Energy Agency said the world oil market is moving back into surplus as Gulf exports recover. Separately, Iraq is reviving an overland route through Syria to move crude by truck. Energy stocks still rose 0.91% on the day.

briefs.headline: Treasury and Fed official split on energy and inflation
briefs.body: Treasury Secretary Bessent and Fed official Austan Goolsbee disagreed over how much the recent energy shock is feeding inflation. The debate matters for rate expectations. Financial stocks fell 1.41% on the session.

briefs.headline: Goldman eyes two ways to profit from an Anthropic IPO
briefs.body: Goldman Sachs is reportedly positioning to benefit from a possible public offering by Anthropic in two separate ways, and other firms are chasing the same business. The report points to a crowded race for large technology listings. Software was flat on the day, down 0.01%.
